summary: This standards-track document specifies the tn3270 URI scheme for resources reached by TN3270 and TN3270E. It updates RFC 1041, RFC 2355, and RFC 1738, which had mentioned it without defining syntax.

eli5.summary: This gives a web-style address for connecting to old IBM-style mainframe terminal sessions.

questions: what is the tn3270 uri scheme
what is the default port for tn3270 uri
subtitle: A web-style address for opening a Telnet 3270 mainframe terminal session.

tldr.problem: The tn3270 URI scheme was mentioned in RFC 1738 and listed in the IANA registry, but nobody had defined its syntax or meaning, so implementers might guess.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6270 defines the form tn3270://userinfo@host:port/, says what each part means, and registers the scheme as Permanent.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 1041, RFC 1738 and RFC 2355, and gives TN3270 and TN3270E sessions a precisely defined address.

today: RFC 6270 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It updates RFC 1041, RFC 1738 and RFC 2355.

sections.title: Why the Scheme Needed a Definition
sections.content:
RFC 6270 specifies the tn3270 URI scheme, used to designate access to resources available through Telnet 3270 mode (TN3270) and Telnet 3270 Enhanced mode (TN3270E).

The scheme was first mentioned in RFC 1738 for URIs that designate "Interactive 3270 emulation sessions". After the URI schemes registry was created under RFC 4395, it was added to the Provisional URI Schemes sub-registry. However, RFC 1738 gave no syntax, no semantics and no registration guidelines for it.

The RFC states the risk plainly: someone might implement the scheme with new, possibly undocumented, syntax just by looking at the IANA registry. This document removes that risk with a precise definition and a registration.
sections.eli5: The name for this kind of address was already on a list, but nobody had said how to write one. So people could have made up their own rules. This document writes down the one true rule.

sections.title: TN3270 and TN3270E
sections.content:
TN3270 is the name for a special mode of a Telnet session (RFC 854). In this mode the IBM 3270 data stream is used to carry data during the session, and the Telnet 3270 Regime option (RFC 1041) enables and negotiates its use.

TN3270E works on a similar principle and is specified in RFC 2355. For background on current practice, the RFC points to RFC 1576. The URI scheme is simply a way to point at a service that speaks either of these.
sections.eli5: Big old IBM computers talk to screens in their own special way. TN3270 is a way to do that talking over a Telnet connection, and TN3270E is a newer take on the same idea.

sections.title: URI Scheme Syntax
sections.content:
The informal (non-normative) form is tn3270://<userinfo>@<host>:<port>/. The userinfo part with its @, and the port part with its :, are OPTIONAL.

The normative rule is written in ABNF (RFC 5234) as tn3270-uri = "tn3270:" "//" authority ["/"]. The authority rule comes from RFC 3986, so the trailing slash is optional too.
sections.eli5: An address starts with the word tn3270, then the name of the computer. You can add a user name in front and a door number after, but you do not have to.

sections.title: URI Scheme Semantics
sections.content:
The host part is REQUIRED and names the host to which the TN3270 or TN3270E connection is to be made. If a port is present, it is the port for the TCP connection to the host. If it is absent, the default port SHALL be 23, as registered in the IANA port registry.

The userinfo part is considered to define information for the Telnet Authentication option (RFC 2941), which might be used during the session.
sections.eli5: The computer name says where to call. If you give no door number, the call goes to door 23. A user name, if you give one, may be used to prove who you are.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Generic URI security issues are covered in Section 7 of RFC 3986. TN3270 and TN3270E are modified forms of Telnet and add no new security issues to a Telnet session, so the only further considerations are those in RFC 4248, the specification of the telnet URI scheme.

The RFC adds that Telnet, TN3270 and TN3270E are inherently insecure. Anyone needing remote login access and related services is encouraged to use a more secure technology, such as Secure Shell (RFC 4251).
sections.eli5: Talking over Telnet is like shouting across a room, since anyone can listen in. The advice is to use a safer method such as Secure Shell when it matters.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content:
IANA updated the registration of the scheme using the template from RFC 4395. The scheme name is tn3270 and its status is Permanent, rather than the earlier provisional listing.

The protocols that use it are Telnet 3270 mode (RFC 1041) and TN3270E (RFC 2355). The contact is the IESG, and the change controller is the IETF. Syntax and semantics point back to Sections 2.1 and 2.2 of this RFC.
sections.eli5: The scheme name moved from a try-out list to the official list, with this document as its instruction sheet.
